heading.en: Most people farmed, yet food was short

hook.en: About 85 per cent of Indians lived in villages and most of them farmed. Why did agriculture stay stagnant for so long?
hook.kn: ಸುಮಾರು 85 ಪ್ರತಿಶತ ಭಾರತೀಯರು ಹಳ್ಳಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ವಾಸಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದರು, ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನವರು ಕೃಷಿಕರು. ಕೃಷಿ ಇಷ್ಟು ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲ ಏಕೆ ಸ್ಥಗಿತವಾಗಿತ್ತು?

objectives.en: Explain the stagnation of colonial agriculture

narration.en: About 85 per cent of Indians lived in villages and most of them farmed. Why did agriculture stay stagnant for so long?
narration.kn: ಸುಮಾರು 85 ಪ್ರತಿಶತ ಭಾರತೀಯರು ಹಳ್ಳಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ವಾಸಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದರು, ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನವರು ಕೃಷಿಕರು. ಕೃಷಿ ಇಷ್ಟು ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲ ಏಕೆ ಸ್ಥಗಿತವಾಗಿತ್ತು?

title.en: Stagnation and the land settlement system

body.en: Indian agriculture under colonial rule was stagnant and often deteriorating. The main cause was the land settlement system, especially the zamindari system in the Bengal Presidency. Zamindars collected rent from cultivators but did little to improve the land; the terms of revenue settlement made them squeeze the farmers.
body.kn: ವಸಾಹತುಶಾಹಿ ಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃಷಿ ಸ್ಥಗಿತವಾಗಿತ್ತು. ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಮುಖ್ಯ ಕಾರಣ ಭೂ ಕಂದಾಯ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ, ವಿಶೇಷವಾಗಿ ಬಂಗಾಳ ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯದ ಜಮೀನ್ದಾರಿ ಪದ್ಧತಿ. ಜಮೀನ್ದಾರರು ರೈತರಿಂದ ಗೇಣಿ ವಸೂಲಿ ಮಾಡಿದರೂ ಭೂಮಿ ಸುಧಾರಣೆಗೆ ಏನೂ ಮಾಡಲಿಲ್ಲ.

points.en: About 85% lived in villages; 70–75% depended on agriculture
Revenue had to be deposited by fixed dates, failing which zamindars lost their rights
Low technology, little irrigation, negligible fertiliser use

title.en: On the board: The zamindari squeeze

say.en: In the Bengal Presidency, the government fixed the revenue it took from each zamindar.
The zamindar collected as much rent as he could from the cultivators.
Rent went up, but no one invested in land, irrigation or fertiliser.
Forced cash crops like indigo and jute fed British mills, not hungry farmers.

body.en: Some areas shifted from food crops to commercial crops such as indigo, jute and cotton, which fed British industries. This raised yields of cash crops in a few places but did little for farmers, who were forced to grow them and still faced hunger.
body.kn: ಕೆಲವು ಪ್ರದೇಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಆಹಾರ ಬೆಳೆಗಳ ಬದಲು ನೀಲಿ, ಸೆಣಬು, ಹತ್ತಿ ಮುಂತಾದ ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ ಬೆಳೆಗಳನ್ನು ಬೆಳೆಯಲಾಯಿತು. ಇದು ಬ್ರಿಟಿಷ್ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಗಳಿಗೆ ನೆರವಾಯಿತು, ರೈತರಿಗಲ್ಲ.

points.en: Commercial crops replaced food crops in some regions
Partition (1947) sent much of the jute-producing land to East Pakistan

title.en: What is left for the cultivator?

caption.en: A cultivator's yearly output is worth ₹V. The zamindar takes r% as rent and inputs cost ₹c. What is left to invest in the land?

narration.en: See how high rent left nothing for investment.

tryThis.en: Raise the rent to 70%. Can the cultivator invest in irrigation?
Why did high rent keep productivity low?
What would happen if the cultivator owned the land?

problem.en: List three reasons why agricultural productivity stayed low in colonial India, in the order a PU answer would present them.

steps.en: Reason 1: the zamindari land settlement system; zamindars extracted rent and did not invest in land.
Reason 2: low level of technology, lack of irrigation and negligible use of fertilisers.
Reason 3: commercialisation that served British industry, not the farmer.

answer.en: Land settlement (zamindari), poor technology and irrigation, and commercialisation for British needs.

points.en: Colonial agriculture was stagnant even though most people depended on it.
points.kn: ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನವರು ಕೃಷಿಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದ್ದರೂ ವಸಾಹತುಶಾಹಿ ಕೃಷಿ ಸ್ಥಗಿತವಾಗಿತ್ತು.

points.en: The zamindari system in Bengal let landlords squeeze farmers without improving land.
points.kn: ಬಂಗಾಳದ ಜಮೀನ್ದಾರಿ ಪದ್ಧತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಜಮೀನ್ದಾರರು ರೈತರನ್ನು ಶೋಷಿಸಿದರು.

points.en: Commercial crops replaced food crops to serve British industries.
points.kn: ಬ್ರಿಟಿಷ್ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕೆಗಳಿಗಾಗಿ ಆಹಾರ ಬೆಳೆಗಳ ಬದಲು ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ ಬೆಳೆಗಳು ಬಂದವು.
